notes: Traditional method: Place the butter in a 1-quart (1-liter) saucepot and melt over low heat, without stirring. Once the butter has melted, it will separate into three layers. Skim off and discard the foamy layer of milk solids floating on top. The clear yellow butter beneath it is the clarified butter. Carefully pour it into a container, leaving the milky liquid at the bottom behind. Use immediately, or cover and refrigerate for up to 10 days or freeze for longer storage.

Refrigerator method: Bring a stockpot of water to a simmer. Place the butter cubes in a heavy-duty resealable kitchen bag and seal. Set the bag in the simmering water to melt the butter. Transfer the bag to an ice-water bath, positioning the bag at an angle with one bottom corner of the bag in the most downward position. Refrigerate until the butter has solidified.
